evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2013 (13 years old), right here: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2017 (fire C50647), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
Unnamed wetland 110 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Soda Creek, about 51 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 52.1999, -122.81902, pull off on Cc162 Spur 1 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 5.0 km SE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 39 m, about 105 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 100 m N of the spot at 1,206 m (52.1644, -122.77517). Water: unnamed wetland 180 m SE (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).

Legal: MU (Management Unit) 5-14, Region 5. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
